rulers.note: Fled to Goguryeo in 436; killed on King Jangsu's orders in 438.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 409: Cliopatria's first Northern Yan year is 410, but Feng Ba took the throne on 6 November 409 (infobox) and the later-yan dossier hands the state over then; the shape is the same 368 cells as Later Yan's 407 shape.

63,533 km2 for 410-425, the Longcheng country (Chaoyang) with western Liaoning and the Tangshan coast. The infobox gives no area (page silent). The page names Longcheng and, in 433, Liaoxi Commandery; it gives no list of commanderies, so the shape stands as Cliopatria's. 'In 416 and 418, Wei clashed with Yan' without a frontier change.

keyframe_review.note: 64,016 km2 for 426-438, six cells more than the 410 shape. Right for 426-432. Liaoxi Commandery (modern Tangshan) is handed to the Wei in 433 (new keyframe northern-yan_433), the state ends in June 436 ('Northern Yan was now at its end, as Feng Hong no longer had any territory of his own'), so 437-438 are not Northern Yan land: Feng Hong was at Goguryeo until his death in 438. Shape unchanged for 426-432; years end 436.

correction.text: Northern Yan without Liaoxi Commandery, handed to the Wei in 433

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 433-436: 'In 433, a succession issue led to Feng Hong's sons handing over Liaoxi Commandery to Wei.' The Feng Hong page places Liaoxi at modern Tangshan, Hebei, and has Feng Chong persuaded to surrender 'around new year 433'. The commandery is drawn as a 100 km disc at Tangshan; 'Liaoxi' as a gazetteer region (Western Liaoning) would also cut Chaoyang.

433: Feng Hong's sons hand Liaoxi Commandery to the Wei. 'In 433, a succession issue led to Feng Hong's sons handing over Liaoxi Commandery to Wei.' The Feng Hong page: Feng Chong, persuaded 'around new year 433', surrendered it.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Northern Yan' 410-438 has two shapes that differ by six cells and runs two years past the 436 end. The page gives no area and no list of commanderies, so the 63-64 thousand km2 shapes could not be compared; the Tangshan disc for Liaoxi is the researcher's reading of 'Liaoxi Commandery (modern Tangshan, Hebei)'. The northern-wei dossier draws the 433 gain with the gazetteer region 'Liaoxi' (Western Liaoning, 365 cells, which includes Chaoyang/Longcheng): that is too large and should use the Tangshan disc. NOT SETTLED: (1) 407 or 409 (infobox: 15 September 407); 409 follows the later-yan dossier, Gao Yun (Murong Yun) ruled 407-409 as Later Yan's last ruler; (2) the Taiwu page (opened for the xia dossier) puts Feng Chong's surrender of Liaoxi in winter 432, the Northern Yan page in 433; (3) the Liu Song vassalage of 435 is recorded on the suzerain side (liu-song-dynasty ledger), none on this state's; (4) relations with Goguryeo, Rouran, Khitan and Kumo Xi: the pages give no dates or territory ('Feng Ba formed good relations'), so no events; (5) Goguryeo is a successor on the infobox but received no land.
